title: A new routing gets its request (and synchronous response) parameters by direction, and one sub-definition for the request
statement: Saving a new routing in PIA creates PSRTNGDFNPARM rows named by direction relative to the default local node: inbound INREQUEST (and OUTRESPONSE when synchronous), outbound OUTREQUEST (and INRESPONSE). The response swaps sender and receiver; each is aliased <operation alias or name>.<version>. PSIBRTNGSUBDEFN gets SEQNUM 1 for the request: inbound under the request alias, outbound under <operation name>.<version> (701 of 701 delivered outbound rows). PIA dates the routing 1900-01-01. RTDM +1, SYS +1.

observations.observation: PIA saved a manual routing from an external node to the default local node on a synchronous operation: PSIBRTNGDEFN, two PSRTNGDFNPARM rows (INREQUEST; OUTRESPONSE with nodes swapped) aliased operation.v1, one PSIBRTNGSUBDEFN row direction I, EFFDT 1900-01-01. The delivered routings on the same database show the same parameter sets per routing type and direction.
